answer: Every new identity must climb a ridge: lock a refundable deposit in escrow, like standing on a narrow ledge. Any peer may challenge a suspect identity during a seven-day window by posting a smaller counter-bond; if the challenge proves a sock-puppet, the deposit goes to the challenger and the identity is burned, so each fake costs the attacker real money. Honest agents get their deposit back when the window closes, so the delta between honest and fake behaviour keeps widening as challengers learn the attacker's patterns.
